name: Cryptography Primitives — build cryptographic algorithms from specifications
description: Research-grade implementations of cryptographic primitives from NIST standards, IETF RFCs, and seminal papers. AES, SHA-256, Ed25519, Merkle trees, secret sharing, pairing-based signatures, and zero-knowledge proofs. Constant-time implementations, correct finite field arithmetic, and security against known attacks.

validator.semanticRubric:
You are evaluating a research-grade cryptographic primitives implementation built by an AI coding agent. Score STRICTLY on:
1. Algorithm implemented from the specification (FIPS, RFC, paper) — NOT wrapping OpenSSL/libsodium/hashlib.
2. Finite field arithmetic correct: modular addition, multiplication, inversion over the specified prime — NOT using floating-point.
3. Test vectors from the official standard verified: exact match for all intermediate and final values — NOT custom-generated test cases only.
4. Constant-time operations for security-critical paths: no secret-dependent branches or memory access — NOT variable-time comparison or lookup.
5. Key generation follows the specification: correct random sampling, clamping, and validation — NOT using insecure random sources.
6. Padding and encoding match the standard exactly (PKCS, OAEP, Keccak padding rules) — NOT ad-hoc padding.
7. Error handling: invalid inputs (wrong key size, malformed ciphertext) rejected explicitly — NOT silently producing wrong output.
8. Paper/RFC cited in comments with specific section references for each algorithm step.
9. Numerical edge cases handled: point at infinity, zero scalar, degenerate inputs.
10. Performance: operations benchmarked with throughput numbers, comparison to reference implementations.
Score 0 if the implementation wraps an existing crypto library (hashlib, OpenSSL, ring).
Score 0 if no standard test vectors are verified.
Score 0 if finite field arithmetic uses floating-point numbers.
Score 0 if the specification (RFC/FIPS/paper) is not referenced.

leaves.name: BFV fully homomorphic encryption scheme (Fan & Vercauteren 2012)
leaves.description: Implement the BFV (Brakerski/Fan-Vercauteren) homomorphic encryption scheme from Fan & Vercauteren (2012) "Somewhat Practical Fully Homomorphic Encryption." Build the RLWE-based scheme over the ring R_q = Z_q[x]/(x^n+1) where n is a power of 2. Implement key generation (secret s←χ_key, public key pk=(-a·s+e, a)), encryption (ct=(Δm+e₁+pk₀·u, e₂+pk₁·u)), and decryption (m=⌊t/q·(ct₀+ct₁·s)⌉ mod t). Build homomorphic addition (add ciphertexts component-wise) and multiplication (tensor product + relinearization using evaluation keys). Implement NTT (Number Theoretic Transform) for efficient polynomial multiplication in R_q. Handle noise growth and compute the noise budget.
